guide.title: Genitourinary & Renal Emergencies
guide.lead: In older adults a UTI may show up only as confusion or a fall. Testicular pain is a race against time. Dialysis patients bring two killers: fluid overload and high potassium. Protect the fistula arm.

sections.title: Common presentations
rows: Confusion, falls, fever or low temperature
Sudden colicky flank pain to the groin, restless, blood in urine
Time critical: best within 6 hours; surgical centre

groups.title: Missed dialysis: fluid
items: Sit up, oxygen, CPAP (see Heart Failure)

groups.title: Missed dialysis: potassium
items: Peaked T waves, then wide QRS, sine wave, arrest

quiz.q: A 78-year-old nursing home resident is newly confused with fever, no urinary symptoms. Suspect:
quiz.explanation: Older adults often lack urinary symptoms.

quiz.q: Missed two dialysis sessions: weak, palpitations, peaked T waves, HR 58. Priority?
options: Hyperkalemia emergency: monitor and transport emergently
quiz.explanation: Can progress to arrest within hours.

quiz.q: Where should you NOT take a BP in a dialysis patient?
Sudden severe testicular pain with vomiting in a 14-year-old:
options: Infection: wait for a doctor's appointment

quiz.q: Colicky flank pain to the groin, can't keep still, blood in the urine:
quiz.explanation: In older patients, rule out aneurysm too.

quiz.q: Fever, flank pain and rigors suggest:

options: Peaked T waves → wide QRS → sine wave → arrest
quiz.explanation: Treat with calcium (ALS) when changes appear.

quiz.q: First drug for hyperkalemia with ECG changes (ALS):
Bleeding from a fistula after dialysis:
A dialysis patient with crackles, edema and SpO₂ 86% after missed sessions:
options: Fluid overload: sit up, oxygen, CPAP, rapid transport

flashcards.question: UTI in older adults
flashcards.answer: May present only with confusion, falls or sepsis, without urinary symptoms.

flashcards.question: Pyelonephritis
flashcards.answer: Fever, flank pain, rigors, vomiting; can become sepsis.

flashcards.question: Renal colic
flashcards.answer: Sudden colicky flank pain to the groin, restless, nausea, blood in urine.

flashcards.question: Fistula arm
flashcards.answer: No BP cuff or IV in the arm with the fistula or graft; use the other arm.

flashcards.question: Missed dialysis: fluid overload
flashcards.answer: Breathlessness, crackles, raised JVP, edema, high BP. Sit up, oxygen, CPAP, transport.

flashcards.question: Hyperkalemia in dialysis patients
flashcards.answer: Bradycardia, block, VF or asystole. ECG: peaked T waves → wide QRS → sine wave → arrest.

flashcards.question: Acute kidney injury causes
flashcards.answer: Pre-renal (low flow), renal (direct damage: toxins, NSAIDs), post-renal (obstruction: stones, prostate).

flashcards.question: Testicular torsion
flashcards.answer: Sudden testicular pain with vomiting: time critical, best within 6 hours. Urgent surgical centre.

critical.scenario: An 82-year-old with dementia and recurrent UTIs is more confused since this morning. BP 90/58, HR 108, temperature 38.6 °C, warm dry skin, tender lower abdomen.
critical.question: Most likely cause?

options.t: Urosepsis: oxygen to target, fluids per protocol, pre-alert, urgent transport

options.f: New confusion with fever and low BP is sepsis.
Fever and low BP point to sepsis.

critical.explanation: Older patients with sepsis decompensate quickly.
critical.kpi: Recognizes urosepsis presenting as altered mental status in an elderly patient

critical.scenario: A dialysis patient missed three sessions: sitting up, can't finish sentences, BP 178/96, RR 32, SpO₂ 86%, crackles, raised JVP, leg edema. Left forearm fistula.
critical.question: Primary problem and plan?

options.t: Fluid overload with pulmonary edema: sit up, oxygen, CPAP, no BP or IV in the left arm, emergency transport for dialysis

critical.explanation: Monitor for hyperkalemia too: get a rhythm strip.
critical.kpi: Recognizes pulmonary edema from fluid overload in a missed-dialysis patient

critical.scenario: A dialysis patient who missed sessions is weak with HR 44. The monitor shows tall peaked T waves and a widening QRS.
critical.question: What's happening and the priority?

options.t: Severe hyperkalemia: pads on, ALS for IV calcium and nebulized salbutamol, emergency transport

options.f: This can arrest at any moment.

critical.explanation: Calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV (or calcium chloride 10% 10 mL) stabilizes the heart.
critical.kpi: Recognizes hyperkalemia ECG changes and arranges membrane-stabilizing treatment
